direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale genuinely doesn't build its world well, as the movie is shot and put together so weirdly that I can't even say it's well made; the direction on a microscale is not good either, as it's all over the place, and the interpersonal scenes are directed so flatly that there's no chemistry in the cast; the storytelling is a mess, as the movie constantly jumps between the present and the past without telling you when, leaving you to piece it all together, and it's so confusing that I genuinely don't know what the conflict or purpose of this movie is beyond a vague character study of a womanizing cellist they try to make feel like James Bond; the tension is so artificially created, with spy espionage sequences that exist for no reason, as it's obvious that Tony Gilroy, who wrote the Bourne movies and directed The Bourne Legacy, is trying to make a spy thriller out of a movie about a cellist

performance.comments: Plays his character fine and shows a good amount of emotional range, but he has no chemistry with the cast and is very flat in many sequences, though I feel like that has more to do with the writing and direction than his performance
Barely in the movie, and I don't understand the purpose of her character, especially in the 15- to 20-minute cold open
Fine, though she's not in the movie that much and doesn't have much to work with
Plays a very 2020s Will Arnett character, the depressed comedic guy, and he plays it well

cast.comments: Very flat, with a lot of monotonous performances that make it feel like it's full of non-actors, with no chemistry whatsoever, as the movie really is all about Pedro Pascal

story.comments: The concept is so unfocused that I can't even tell you what it is, as it's basically a character study of a cellist, but they make the cellist feel like James Bond, which is such a weird concept for a movie; the plot structure is the biggest issue, constantly jumping between the present and the past without telling you when, so you have to piece it together through context clues like a Hillary for President 2016 sign or a 2010 gala while sitting through boring dialogue, and while I'm a big fan of 'show, don't tell,' at some point a movie has to tell you something, so this much subtlety turns the whole thing into homework; character writing is bad, especially for a character study, as the cellist is painted so poorly that I didn't care about him at all, even when they show him having empathy toward someone, and the rest of the characters aren't any better

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is clunky and forced at moments, coming off as monotonous when the characters deliver it; the humor shows up a decent amount and somewhat lands, even though the movie isn't supposed to be funny; the symbolism is unclear, since the conflict and messaging are never clearly defined, though there's a retrospective on his life showing how he runs away from his problems because of the trauma from his upbringing with his father, along with the relationship he wants with a certain person, but it doesn't land when the character isn't well written; the foreshadowing builds up a reveal toward the end decently well, but the weird structure limits it, as something gets alluded to and then only paid off a while later, so you have to remember what they said earlier

score.comments: Objectively well composed, but it makes zero sense for this movie, as the collective of composers delivers cues that sound like The Dark Knight or a James Bond thriller, making it feel like a spy espionage or hardcore action movie, and while I get that he's recording scores for real movies that transport him back to points in his life, it still makes no sense for a movie about a cellist

cinematography.comments: Shot so weirdly, with a lot of wide-angle and panning shots, a fly-on-the-wall feel at points, and spy-style following shots that try to make it feel like James Bond for a movie about a cellist, though the shots of him at the beach and driving through the tunnel are actually well shot

editing.comments: Edited very poorly, as it doesn't seamlessly transition between the flashbacks and the present day, leaving you to piece together when the flashbacks are happening, and the cut feels so bloated

sound.comments: Genuinely the best part of the movie, as it's very crisp and technically sound for an orchestra movie, making it feel like you're in a booth recording the instruments

production_design.comments: Shot in cool places, from sound recording studios and symphony halls to a lot of regal, big houses that make it feel kind of like a Bond movie, though the Chicago sequence clearly wasn't filmed at the actual Chicago Symphony Center

costumes.comments: A lot of suits and the attire you would see in an orchestra

review.pacing: Unbearably slow, as its two hours and seven minutes feel like three hours because of the weird structure and boring concept, so they needed to cut 20 minutes from its many storylines and make the flashbacks more obvious, though the last 30 minutes are somewhat satisfying as all the ideas converge like a web at the end
review.climax: Executed well, giving the movie decent emotional closure, even if it isn't the best
review.tone: I have no idea what this movie is going for tonally, as it's a character study of a cellist that randomly turns into a spy espionage movie at moments, when it could have just been a drama instead of trying to be James Bond
review.final_notes: Saw a screening at Austin Film Festival
review.overall: Overall, 'Behemoth!' is a complete mess and a very boring movie, as its weird, all-over-the-place structure and extreme subtlety make it feel like homework to piece together, while its random spy espionage sequences and thriller score make no sense for a character study of a cellist, leaving me unsure what the movie is even about
